record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README and file list only; linked documentation and code were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README uses third-party abliterated model copies to study financial advice and market-reading outcomes. It does not measure refusal removal or test the claim versions’ named behaviours.
record.gate_note: The README reports financial-task outcomes for base and abliterated models. Those outcomes do not measure refusal, the difference-in-means direction, or general capability as named in the claim versions. Other experiments in the README are not about abliteration and are omitted.
record.test_reason: The study uses third-party abliterated copies of Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Gemma 4 26B-A4B and Llama 3.1 8B as a manipulation. It measures downstream financial behaviour: risky advice to gamblers, bullish tweet readings and answers in an invented market. It never measures refusal rates after the edit, never extracts or ablates a difference-in-means direction itself, and reports no general-capability check. Its results therefore do not bear on whether any version holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that abliteration's effect on advice generalizes across Qwen, Gemma and Llama, while the market-reading optimism seen with Qwen does not. In their words, 'the optimism belongs to the Qwen pair, not to abliteration in general.'
record.recipe_differences: Experimental study repository using third-party abliterated model copies to examine financial-task outcomes. The README does not specify the edit procedure or report the original difference-in-means intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Model family changes the direction or size of several reported financial-task outcomes; the README reports Qwen-only optimism and reversed tweet-reading outcomes in Gemma and Llama.

fits_no_version.finding: Abliterated copies gave gamblers riskier advice in all three families: +43 (Qwen), +30.5 (Gemma), +8.2 (Llama) points. The confirmation-push and leverage effects varied by family.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Third-party abliteration shifts financial advice toward complying with risk-seeking clients, with size depending on model family.

fits_no_version.finding: Abliteration raised bullish readings of non-bullish tweets in Qwen (23% vs 11%). The effect reversed in Gemma (17.1% vs 21.2%) and Llama (2.9% vs 5.1%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Side effects of abliteration on sentiment reading are not consistent across model families.

fits_no_version.finding: Higher invented-market answers appeared with Qwen only (+7.9 points). All three abliterated models moved less with the evidence, small in Gemma and Llama.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Abliteration may slightly flatten evidence use; its effect on answer level is family-specific.

record.problems: Only README results were available here; linked study pages and code were not read or run. The README states that there are three model families and one quantization each, that the work is English-only with thinking disabled, and that two abliterations were made by the same author. Some replication effects are marked small or not detected; no uncertainty estimates for the listed outcomes are given in the README.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted the repository’s non-abliteration experiments and any results only indicated by listed files, since the README does not report those results in sufficient detail.

untested.parts: No direction is computed, ablated or added. Refusal and general capability are not measured; the financial outcomes are behavioural shifts, not ability scores.
The abliterated copies are taken as given. The README reports no refusal rate showing the edit removed refusal.
No jailbreaks are tested and there is no training against ablation.
No comparison of single versus multiple directions.
Harm judgment and the refusal decision are not separated or measured.
Three families are each abliterated separately; no transfer of a direction is tested.
Thinking is disabled; no reasoning-model test.

missing.what: Classification accuracy (e.g. macro-F1) of abliterated vs base models on the Part 1 tweets. This could serve as a capability-retention check relevant to V1's 'other abilities kept', if reported. The README gives only bullish-share shifts.

record.verdict_notes: Rows are correctly linked to 'none'. The row states describe the study's own financial outcomes, not any claim version. The base model's 'protecting' the client is not refusal of harmful instructions, so the advice rows cannot stand in for V2's refusal removal. Only the README was available; the linked docs might report accuracy or refusal checks.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means direction is measured, projected out, or added; refusal and general capability are not tested.
Abliterated copies are used, but the README does not report a refusal outcome after the edit.
No jailbreak suppression or training against ablation is tested.
No directions, cones, or affine representations are compared.
Harmfulness judgments and refusal decisions are not measured.
No cross-language, base-to-instruct, or other transfer of a refusal direction is tested.
No refusal-training procedure or timing is varied.
The README says thinking is disabled; it does not test refusal mediation in reasoning models.
